question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations 2024, the Dissolution Period of an AIF scheme is subject to what maximum cap?

answer.text: Not more than 1 year, extendable by 1 further year.
Not more than 2 years, extendable by 2 further years.
Unlimited, subject to quarterly SEBI approvals.
Not more than the ORIGINAL TENURE of the scheme, and not extendable upon its expiry.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 12 (SEBI AIF Second Amendment 2024): 'The dissolution period of a scheme of an AIF shall not be more than the original tenure of the scheme and shall not be extended in any manner upon expiry of the dissolution period.' During dissolution, no new investments and no fresh commitments are allowed. The Trap: 1-year, 2-year caps are reasonable-sounding but wrong. 'Unlimited' contradicts the express non-extension rule. The cap is tied to the ORIGINAL scheme tenure, a dynamic that surprises many candidates. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the same 2024 rule. This is a recent change — pre-2024 study material does not cover it; expect it to appear as a high-frequency testable item. Manager's Pro-Tip: If your scheme's original tenure was 8 years, the dissolution period can be up to 8 years — but you must file an Information Memorandum through a merchant banker with SEBI BEFORE expiry of the liquidation period. Plan the MB engagement well in advance.
